topics.label: Introduction and learning aims
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture's place in the series and sets out its scope and learning outcomes.

topics.label: Molecular changes driving cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how changes in cellular genetic programs can confer properties that enable clonal expansion and tumor formation.

topics.label: Stemness, cell of origin and tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell's position in a tissue hierarchy affects its capacity to initiate and sustain a tumor.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness in cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can give mutation-bearing cells the stem-like properties needed for tumor development.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive surrounding cells as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

topics.label: Methods for studying cancer evolution and cell interactions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how molecular profiling of tissue specimens can reveal cancer's evolutionary history and interactions within its microenvironment.

topics.label: Converging conditions for malignant outgrowth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic develops an integrated account of the conditions permitting malignant evolution and extends it to developmental susceptibility in childhood cancers.

topics.label: Lecture close and next session
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and announces the forthcoming session on therapy.
